signals.title: Schneider Electric Enerlin'X IFE and eIFE
signals.summary: Schneider Electric is aware of vulnerabilities in its Enerlin'X IFE and Enerlin'X eIFE products. The Enerlin'X IFE and eIFE products https://www.se.com/ww/en/product-range/62413-enerlinx-ife-eife-ifm/#products are used to enable Masterpact, PowerPact, and Compact circuit breakers to be connected to an Ethernet network.

signals.title: Siemens Teamcenter Visualization
signals.summary: Siemens Teamcenter Visualization contains multiple file parsing vulnerabilities that could be triggered when the application reads files in WRL format. If a user is tricked to open a malicious file with any of the affected products, this could lead the application to crash or potentially lead to arbitrary code execution. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.
signals.relevance: Official CISA ICS advisory; maritime deployment not asserted

signals.title: Siemens COMOS
signals.summary: COMOS is affected by XXE injection vulnerabilities that could allow an attacker to extract arbitrary application files. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Siemens recommends specific countermeasures for products where fixes are not, or not yet available.
signals.relevance: Official CISA ICS advisory; maritime deployment not asserted

signals.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM ROX II
signals.summary: The CLI feature in the web interface of RUGGEDCOM ROX II devices is vulnerable to cross-site request forgery (CSRF), which could allow an attacker to perform administrative actions if an authenticated user is tricked into accessing a malicious link. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.
signals.relevance: Official CISA ICS advisory; maritime deployment not asserted

signals.title: Siemens CPCI85 Central Processing/Communication
signals.summary: The SICAM A8000 CP-8031 and CP-8050 devices are affected by a vulnerability that could allow an attacker with physical access to the device to decrypt the firmware. Siemens has released new firmware and hardware versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Both the firmware and the hardware update are required to fix the vulnerability. For details see the section "Additional Information".
signals.relevance: Official CISA ICS advisory; maritime deployment not asserted

signals.title: Schneider Electric Vijeo Designer and EcoStruxure Machine Expert (Update A)
signals.summary: Schneider Electric is aware of a vulnerability in its Vijeo Designer product. The Vijeo Designer https://www.se.com/ww/en/product-range/1054-vijeo-designer-hmi-software/ product is HMI Configuration Software compatible with Harmony and Magelis HMI. Vijeo Designer software offers functions such as multimedia capabilities and remote access for more efficiency. Failure to apply the remediations provided below may risk privilege escalation, which could result in unauthorized access to workstation resources.
signals.relevance: Official CISA ICS advisory; maritime deployment not asserted

signals.title: Siemens Software Center

signals.title: Siemens Industrial Software Products
signals.summary: On October 21, 2026, the Node.js project released security updates addressing a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, commonly referred to as "Node2Shell" (tracked as CVE-2026-111497). The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write that could allow a remote attacker to cause memory corruption and potentially execute arbitrary code. This advisory covers the status of impact of various Siemens software products.

This vulnerability poses a risk only during setup and installation phase of the affected applications downloaded e.g. via OSD (Online Software Delivery).
signals.relevance: Official CISA ICS advisory; maritime deployment not asserted

signals.title: Siemens SIMATIC S7-PLCSIM
signals.summary: Affected products do not properly sanitize user-controllable input when parsing project files. This could allow an attacker to cause a type confusion and execute arbitrary code within the affected application. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Siemens is preparing further fix versions and recommends specific countermeasures for products where fixes are not, or not yet available.
signals.relevance: Official CISA ICS advisory; maritime deployment not asserted

signals.title: Siemens Engineering Platforms
signals.summary: Affected products do not properly restrict access permissions to a local Windows Named Pipe and do not properly sanitize user-controllable input sent to that Named Pipe. This could allow a local authenticated attacker to cause a type confusion and execute arbitrary code within the affected application and its privileges. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.
